comparisons.peer_topic: 2024 Impairment and Depreciation Charges Impacting Gross Margin
comparisons.peer_summary: Consolidated gross margin decreased by $4.4 billion in 2024 compared to 2023, primarily driven by $3.3 billion in impairment and accelerated depreciation charges related to manufacturing assets exceeding capacity for the Intel 7 process node, as well as $922 million in Gaudi AI accelerator inventory-related charges.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and INTC disclose material charges impacting gross margin, though in opposite directions and for different asset types. MU's 2023 gross margin of -9% was negatively impacted by 'charges to write down inventories,' which contributed to the subsequent 2024 recovery as those lower-cost assets were sold. In contrast, INTC's 2024 gross margin decreased by $4.4 billion due to '$3.3 billion in impairment charges and accelerated depreciation' of manufacturing assets (Intel 7 process node) and '$922 million in Gaudi AI accelerator inventory-related charges.' Both companies identify significant one-time or structural charges related to asset valuation (inventory vs. PP&E) as critical factors in their reported gross margin performance.

sentences.text: Our consolidated gross margin percentage improved to 22% for 2024 from negative 9% for 2023, as a result of improvements in margins for both DRAM and NAND products, primarily due to increases in average selling prices, and manufacturing cost reductions, the effects of charges to write down inventories to their NRV in 2023 and lower costs in 2024 from the sale of inventories written down in 2023 (as detailed in "Inventory NRV write-downs" below).
Our consolidated gross margin in 2024 decreased by $4.4 billion, or 20%, compared to 2023 due primarily to higher 2024 impairment charges and accelerated depreciation.

Our 2024 gross margin also decreased due to lower revenue, higher unit cost primarily from an increased mix of Intel 4 and Intel 7 products, higher period charges due to $922 million in Gaudi AI accelerator inventory-related charges recognized in 2024, and higher factory start-up costs.

comparisons.peer_summary: Inventory provisions and sales of previously written-down items had an unfavorable impact on gross margin of 2.7% in fiscal year 2024 and 7.5% in fiscal year 2023.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and NVDA explicitly disclose the net financial impact of inventory provisions and the sale of previously written-down inventory on their consolidated gross margins for 2024. MU reports a 22% gross margin improvement in 2024 compared to -9% in 2023, driven by 'lower costs in 2024 from the sale of inventories written down in 2023,' whereas NVDA quantifies the drag from these same mechanisms, noting an 'unfavorable impact of 2.7% in fiscal year 2024' from 'inventory provisions and sales of items previously written down.' While both cite inventory dynamics as a key margin driver, MU highlights the positive cost benefit from prior write-downs contributing to a strong recovery, while NVDA highlights the continued, albeit reduced, negative drag from these provisions.

sentences.text: Our consolidated gross margin percentage improved to 22% for 2024 from negative 9% for 2023, as a result of improvements in margins for both DRAM and NAND products, primarily due to increases in average selling prices, and manufacturing cost reductions, the effects of charges to write down inventories to their NRV in 2023 and lower costs in 2024 from the sale of inventories written down in 2023 (as detailed in "Inventory NRV write-downs" below).
The net effect on our gross margin from inventory provisions and sales of items previously written down was an unfavorable impact of 2.7% in fiscal year 2024 and 7.5% in fiscal year 2023.

peer_results.rationale: Candidate qcom_2024_7_D011 and qcom_2024_7_D024 only state that gross margin remained flat and do not provide the specific drivers, such as inventory write-downs or ASP changes, that MU discloses. Without specific discussion of the same drivers, they are not substantively comparable.
